title: Add event-driven delta projections

scope.assurance_scope: PCSM Python-v1 event-driven delta-projection capability assessment for the exact current admitted source forest
scope.implementation_delta: Reuse the current-head ProjectionDeltaCheckpointStore@1 and its PortalImplementationDaemon integration. The store canonically serializes a JSON-object projection, binds it to an EventCursor, records only sorted top-level set/remove deltas, derives SHA-256 content identities, atomically publishes changed checkpoints, and makes unchanged projection/cursor pairs zero-write. The daemon binds its runtime checkpoint to the closed asi-117 event-driven-delta-checkpoint-runtime requirement. No PCSM wrapper, alternative projection head, source-map authority, source/test mutation, M2/M3 mutation, or task materialization was introduced under this exact receipt-only authority.
scope.non_promotion_reason: The reusable implementation is a generic supervisor runtime checkpoint, not a canonical PCSM projection contract. The exact current source forest has no PCSM ProjectionRoot/projection schema, named PCSM projection identity, aggregate PCSM SourceLinkReceipt/source-map CID, or concrete source-forest projection result. The selected focused fixtures exercise generic synthetic event/projection records, and the full 13-test event-runtime module cannot complete in the sealed environment because duckdb is unavailable for six daemon-integration tests. This receipt therefore preserves the generic capability and its evidence boundary without promoting it to a PCSM semantic projection, source-forest execution, completion, or admission authority.

selected_existing_authority.minimum_delta_reason: ProjectionDeltaCheckpointStore@1 is the smallest current-head implementation that already couples an event cursor with a deterministic projection delta and durable checkpoint. PortalImplementationDaemon is its existing owner-side consumer. Replacing either with a PCSM wrapper or competing projection store would exceed this receipt-only dispatch and duplicate the generic authority.

components.role: Atomic, lock-protected generic projection/cursor checkpoint. It validates the record schema and self-content identity on read; rejects wrong-stream, backward, and same-position re-anchored cursors; and emits deterministic top-level deltas plus runtime-projection and checkpoint SHA-256 identities.

Existing generic runtime owner that writes the compact result/state projection with the latest canonical event cursor, loads only matching schema/requirement records, and quarantines/replaces invalid checkpoint material before retrying persistence.

determinism_and_binding.available_binding: Canonical JSON uses sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, and allow_nan=false. The delta orders set keys and removed keys; projection_id and checkpoint_id are SHA-256 content identities; EventCursor parsing and monotonicity checks bind the checkpoint to one ordered event stream; the checkpoint schema is explicit @1; changed records are written through temporary file, fsync, atomic replace, and parent-directory fsync; identical inputs return write_count=0.
determinism_and_binding.missing_binding: No selected record names a PCSM projection schema/version, canonical PCSM projection CID, exact PCSM repository/tree/source-map CID, SourceLinkReceipt, or source-map-bound semantic result. Generic SHA-256 content IDs are not CIDv1 identities and do not meet those missing PCSM bindings.
determinism_and_binding.authority_boundary: The selected components persist and replay generic supervisor-runtime state only. They do not establish semantic correctness, choose a canonical PCSM identity, authorize aliases, mutate PCSM source, create tasks, admit a projection, authorize M2/M3 work, or decide completion/promotion. The exact PCSM configuration's disabled objective refill remains fail-closed.

source_inventory.role: Current-head ProjectionDeltaCheckpointStore@1: canonical serialization, sorted set/remove delta generation, schema/self-identity validation, cursor fencing, atomic publication, and unchanged zero-write result.

Current-head generic daemon integration: closed requirement identifier, runtime result projection, latest-event cursor checkpointing, validation on load, invalid-checkpoint quarantine/retry, and runtime delta reporting.

Thirteen generic event-runtime vectors: cursor replay/rotation, two-phase acknowledgement, watcher fallback, bounded metadata, zero unchanged writes, daemon cleanup/wake isolation, low-CPU idle behavior, task-identity preservation, and lease-wake exclusion.
Required PCSM-root structured-output positive/negative boundary suite. It is recorded separately and is not relabelled as event-driven delta-projection coverage.

focused_generic_event_delta_tests.command: PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin HOME=<fresh ipfs-accelerate-validation-home-pcsm085-direct-*> XDG_CACHE_HOME=$HOME/.cache XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.config XDG_DATA_HOME=$HOME/.local/share XDG_STATE_HOME=$HOME/.local/state PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=ipfs_accelerate_py /usr/bin/python3.12 -m pytest -q test/api/test_agent_supervisor_event_driven_runtime.py -k '<seven named low-level/runtime-runner vectors>'
focused_generic_event_delta_tests.environment: Authoritative sealed Python 3.12.3 with pytest 8.1.1, prescribed PATH, fresh private HOME/XDG root, user-site disabled, and accelerator source only on PYTHONPATH.
positive_coverage: Gapless exactly-once canonical event-cursor replay across restart and log rotation, with duplicate-tail coalescing.
All runtime wake kinds use canonical cursors and two-phase acknowledgement; event-loop runner wakes and closes correctly; bounded metadata precedes projection work.

ProjectionDeltaCheckpointStore computes the expected deterministic set/remove delta, advances its cursor, reloads the persisted projection, and leaves reordered identical input untouched with write_count=0.
negative_coverage: Acknowledgement is required before a semantic wake stops replaying; re-delivery of an acknowledged canonical revision is a no-op.
An unsupported native watcher falls back to the blocking timer rather than claiming native event support; bounded metadata truncates oversized trees.

The selected store vector demonstrates that an unchanged reordered projection/cursor cannot cause an extra atomic write. Source-inspected negative fences reject malformed/oversized records, unsupported schema, forged checkpoint identity, non-object projection/cursor, wrong stream, backward cursor, and a changed cursor anchor at the same position.
focused_generic_event_delta_tests.scope_limit: These are generic controlled fixtures, not an exact-PCSM ProjectionRoot or source-map-bound projection result. The cursor-fence source behavior is measured by inspection; it is not claimed as separately executed negative-vector coverage.
